newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong people "neutral" on Beijing rule - poll.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong people "neutral" on Beijing rule - poll.

text.p: Most people in Hong Kong are neutral towards its transfer to Chinese rule, an opinion poll said on Wednesday.

More than half, or 58.3 percent, of those interviewed in the University of Hong Kong's latest poll had "neutral" words to describe the historic event, 31.3 percent felt positive, 4.5 percent were negative, and 3.2 percent were ambivalent.
Hong Kong returned to Beijing's control on Tuesday after 156 years under British colonial rule.
Hong Kong people were almost evenly split whether they were proud to become Chinese nationals, the poll showed.
Some 45.7 percent said they were not proud, and 46.6 said they were proud.
There was a far stronger consensus on the way the actual handover was handled. About 72 percent said they were satisfied.

Only 5.9 percent said Britain did not give enough democracy to Hong Kong during its century and a half of largely autocratic rule. Britain began introducing democracy here only in the 1990s, following an 1989 anti-democracy crackdown in Beijing.
About 26 percent of those polled said they found no fault with the former British administration.
